# Introduction

`gamdid` is an R package for DD analysis on single cell proteomics data.
It is designed to detect and visualize distributional differences between
two or more experimental conditions, going beyond conventional mean-based 
differential  abundance (DA) methods. `gamdid` is sensitive to any form of 
distributional difference (shape and location).

A key advantage of `gamdid` is its interpretable visualization, which links 
statistical inference to the specific regions of the distribution that differ 
between groups. This allows users to not only identify differentially distributed 
features, but also to understand the nature of the distributional difference. 
Additionally, `gamdid` supports omnibus testing across more than two groups, 
followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons corrected for multiple testing using 
stagewise testing.

`gamdid` builds on the `mgcv` CRAN package for fitting generalized additive models 
and on the Bioconductor package `stageR` for stagewise testing. It provides easy 
integration with `SingleCellExperiment`, `SummarizedExperiment` and `QFeatures` 
classes, making it straightforward to incorporate into existing single-cell 
proteomics workflows.

All methodological details underlying `gamdid`, including the Poisson GAM 
framework, the Wald-type test for distributional differences, and the p-value 
aggregation strategy, are described in our preprint [@Beerland2026].


This vignette provides a step-by-step workflow for using `gamdid` for
dimensionality reduction of omics data. The main function are:


1. `compDistr` performs comparisons between the different groups of the covariate
of interest.

2. `visFit` visualizes the GAM fits used for inference and marks differential 
regions with grey shades

Here we apply `gamdid` on single cell proteomics data.


# Package installation

`mgcv` can be installed through CRAN.
`stageR` can be installed from Bioconductor, `gamdid` can be installed from github

```{r, eval=FALSE}
if(!requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("mgcv")

```

```{r setup}
library(gamdid)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(msqrob2)
library(mgcv)
library(lme4)
library(reformulas)
library(harmonicmeanp)
library(stageR)
library(scpdata)
```

# Load in dataset

We use single cell proteomics data acquired by the Slavov Lab. It contains quantitative information of melanoma cells and monocytes at PSM, peptide and protein level. 

```{r}
leduc <- leduc2022_pSCoPE()

# save memory and computing time
leduc <- getWithColData(leduc, i = "proteins_processed")[1:200,]
```

Leduc is a `QFeatures` object with 138 assays, we will use the `proteins_processed` assay containing quantitative data for 2844 proteins and 1543 single-cells.

# DD for comparing two groups

We use the `compDistr` function for the DD analysis.

```{r}
leduc_dd <- compDistr(object = leduc, covariate = "SampleType")
```
Explore the results

```{r}
rowData(leduc_dd)
metadata(leduc_dd)
```
Visualize interesting features
```{r}
# when you are interested in looking at the most significant features
dd_sorted <- rowData(leduc_dd)[order(rowData(leduc_dd)$SampleTypeMelanoma_VS_SampleTypeMonocyte),]
visFit(object = leduc_dd, feature = rownames(dd_sorted)[1], plot = "hist")
```

# DD for comparing more than two groups

```{r}
leduc_threewaycomp <- leduc[,!is.na(leduc$Field)]
leduc_threewaycomp$Field <- as.factor(leduc_threewaycomp$Field)
leduc_dd_threeway <- compDistr(object = leduc_threewaycomp, covariate = "Field", adjust = "contrastwise")
```

Explore the results

```{r}
rowData(leduc_dd_threeway)
metadata(leduc_dd_threeway)
```
```{r}
# when you are interested in looking at the most significant features
dd_threeway_sorted <- rowData(leduc_dd_threeway[order(rowData(leduc_dd_threeway)$omnibus),])
visFit(object = leduc_dd_threeway, feature = rownames(dd_threeway_sorted)[1], plot = "hist")
```
